items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: and Artie Shaw was very smart at fixing arrangements too.

ctx.x: Isn’t it good to write something or do something that you know communicates to other musicians, even in other genres? That should make you feel good.

It does but that happens after the fact. I mean when you’re writing it you’re not thinking of that, you’re just doing something that you like that appeals to you. You write it out and did an arrangement for the band, that’s the kick, when you hear it back the first time. And then as it goes on it gets better because they play it better. They learn it and everybody seems to fit their part and get it to blend better and everything’s smoother. So that’s the thing about arranging for a band. You see it evolve and get…
And of course, you know, all bands have a tendency to be stereotyped for one or two favorite tunes and sometimes it isn’t even the best tune.
